title: Browser Feature & Client-Side Advanced
description: Browser features, DOM behavior, and client-side isolation boundaries.

attacks.name: DOM clobbering
attacks.desc: An injected element ID or name can shadow JavaScript globals and alter client-side logic.
attacks.prevention: Avoid relying on clobberable global names; use explicit DOM queries and validate returned node types.

attacks.name: Shadow DOM XSS
attacks.desc: Unsafe rendering inside a shadow root can still create XSS; shadow DOM does not sanitize content.
attacks.prevention: Treat shadow-root insertion as a real HTML sink and sanitize or encode untrusted content before rendering.

attacks.name: Angular sandbox escape
attacks.desc: Older AngularJS expression contexts may allow code execution when untrusted content reaches a template.
attacks.prevention: Upgrade unsupported AngularJS code and avoid compiling untrusted strings as framework templates.

attacks.name: Vue/React escape
attacks.desc: Unsafe HTML escape hatches such as v-html or dangerouslySetInnerHTML can render attacker-controlled markup.
attacks.prevention: Use framework text rendering by default; sanitize any content passed to v-html or dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

attacks.name: CSS exfiltration
attacks.desc: Injected CSS may infer attribute values through conditional selectors and observable resource loads.
attacks.prevention: Do not let users inject arbitrary CSS into pages that display secrets; use scoped design tokens and a restrictive CSP.

attacks.name: Font-based exfil
attacks.desc: Font selection and glyph loading can form a side channel for characters rendered in protected text.
attacks.prevention: Limit untrusted styles and external font loads near sensitive text, and review font requests as potential side channels.

attacks.name: CSP bypass
attacks.notes: JSONP, weak base-uri, nonce reuse, policy interactions
attacks.desc: Weak CSP sources, nonces, or policy structure can leave script execution paths open.

attacks.name: Trusted Types bypass
attacks.desc: Trusted Types helps cover DOM injection sinks, but uncovered sinks or policy misuse can still allow injection.

attacks.name: SRI bypass
attacks.notes: No hash, or hash on wrong file
attacks.desc: Missing or mismatched integrity metadata leaves third-party scripts open to replacement without hash detection.

attacks.name: iframe sandbox escape
attacks.desc: Combining script execution and same-origin access in an iframe sandbox can undermine its intended isolation.

attacks.name: Drag & drop injection
attacks.desc: Untrusted drag-and-drop data can become active content if the application inserts it without validation.

attacks.name: Clipboard hijack
attacks.desc: A page with enough clipboard permission can replace copied content and mislead a later paste.

attacks.name: WebRTC IP leak
attacks.desc: WebRTC candidate gathering may reveal network addresses depending on browser privacy protections.

attacks.name: Sensor/Bluetooth/USB abuse
attacks.desc: Device APIs expose sensitive capabilities only under supported browser security and permission rules.

attacks.name: Service worker takeover
attacks.desc: A service worker registered under an overly broad scope can intercept later same-origin requests.

attacks.name: PWA manifest abuse
attacks.desc: An unsafe PWA start URL or manifest field can redirect launches or misrepresent the installed app.
